passages.title: Descriptive Text 01
passages.text: The art room has large tables, jars of paint, and shelves of paper. Students use the room to draw, paint, and make posters.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 02
passages.text: Behind the school, a small pond has clear water and green plants. Fish swim below the leaves, and birds often stop at its edge.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 03
passages.text: The new bus stop has a long roof, comfortable seats, and a clear route map. Passengers can wait out of the rain and check where their buses go.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 04
passages.text: The town library has books in two languages. It also has a reading corner for children and quiet desks for students. People of different ages use it every day.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 05
passages.text: A small public playground stands between two apartment buildings. It has swings for children, a walking path, and benches for adults. In the evening, neighbours gather there to spend time together.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 06
passages.text: At the community herb garden, small labels name each plant and describe its everyday uses. Volunteers show visitors how to care for the herbs, while families walk between the planting beds. Some school groups come with notebooks to record what they learn.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 07
passages.text: The pottery workshop is housed in an old warehouse. Bright shelves hold bowls and cups made by local artists. Behind a glass wall, visitors can watch the artists shape wet clay and paint finished pieces. On weekends, short classes allow visitors to try making simple pottery themselves.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 08
passages.text: Although surrounded by busy roads, Merdeka Square feels calm inside. Tall trees shade its walking paths, and a low fountain softens the sound of traffic. Office workers sit on benches during lunch, while children walk with their families in the late afternoon.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 09
passages.text: The seafood market near the harbor begins its activities before sunrise. Fishers carry fresh catches to open stalls, and buyers compare the fish, prawns, and crabs on display. Nearby food sellers prepare simple breakfasts for workers. By seven o'clock, the narrow lanes are crowded with people buying, selling, and eating.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 10
passages.text: The old stone bridge crosses a shallow river at the edge of town. Its original arches remain, but a new walkway and handrails make it safer for pedestrians. Information boards explain how traders used the bridge a century ago. Today, local residents cross it daily, while visitors stop to learn about its history.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 11
passages.text: At the edge of the school grounds, an unused water tower has been converted into a small astronomy centre. The lower room contains models of planets and a collection of student-made star charts. Upstairs, a telescope points toward the night sky. Science classes use the centre during the day, and local families join supervised sky-watching sessions on selected evenings. Although the tower's brick exterior remains unchanged, its interior now supports activities the building was never originally designed for.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 12
passages.text: In the centre of town stands the Amerta Theatre, built in the 1930s. During a recent restoration, workers repaired the faded ceiling paintings and kept the original wooden seats in the front rows. New lighting and safer exits were added without changing the shape of the main hall. The theatre now hosts school plays, traditional dance performances, and weekend concerts. Visitors who arrive early can also view photographs showing the building at different points in its history.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 13
passages.text: Along the northern coast, a raised wooden boardwalk winds through a strip of mangrove trees. At high tide, water covers the roots, while small fish move among them. Information signs describe how mangroves provide shelter for marine life and help reduce the force of waves. Several viewing platforms allow visitors to observe birds without entering the muddy ground below. Local guides sometimes lead students along the path, pointing out changes between the wet and dry seasons. The boardwalk makes an otherwise difficult environment easier to explore while keeping visitors on a designated route.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 14
passages.text: The village weaving studio opens onto a courtyard where bundles of cotton thread hang in the shade. Inside, older artisans work at wooden looms, producing cloth with patterns passed down through their families. Apprentices sit nearby, learning how to prepare dyes and tighten the threads. A small display area explains the meaning of the traditional patterns, and visitors can purchase finished cloth directly from the makers. The steady sound of the looms continues throughout the day as experienced and younger weavers work side by side.

passages.title: Descriptive Text 15
passages.text: Five years ago, a section of the riverbank behind the market was covered by an abandoned parking area. Today, a narrow public park follows the curve of the water. Rain gardens collect runoff from nearby streets, and native grasses grow between the walking paths. Small signs explain why the vegetation is left tall in some places. Commuters use the path as a shortcut in the morning, while residents sit near the river after work. Parts of the old pavement remain visible beneath the new benches, reminding visitors of the site's former use. Although the park is modest in size, it connects the market, the bus terminal, and several neighbourhood streets.
